transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start time: 13:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Ethan R., Maya P., Jordan L., Samira K., Liam O'Neill, plus company-wide participants

[00:00] Ethan R: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the Q2 priorities. I know folks are remote, so feel free to drop reactions.
[00:23] Speaker 1 (Audience): wave emoji, hi Ethan.
[00:30] Maya P: morning — sorry I was on a bug triage til the prior minute. We'll start with reliability, i think that's top of mind.
[01:02] Jordan L: quick note — the postmortem for last week's degradation is up in Confluence, link in the chat. We had a KV cache thrash that cascaded into higher tail latency; sometimes the transcription spells that as K V cash, so forgive the notes.
[01:40] Samira K: thanks Jordan, and big picture, customers care about two things: predictability and security. We've seen more askers for private deployments, V P C options, and on-prem runway.
[02:10] Ethan R: yes. So the agenda: 1) reliability investments; 2) product launches (Console and Optimize updates); 3) commercial motions for Dedicated; 4) people/hiring; 5) open Q&A.
[03:02] Liam O'Neill: i'll take Dedicated pricing — finance and I have been iterating on three SKUs, and we think there is room to be clearer on burst capacity and reserved throughput. Will share slides after.
[03:40] Speaker 2: mic check.
[04:05] Maya P: on reliability, engineering will prioritize three workstreams: a) KV cache eviction improvements, b) improved autoscaling signals for Dedicated pools, c) index warmup for private deployments so startups don't hit cold-start tail. We've got a runway of six weeks for the first ship.
[04:38] Ethan R: that's good. Do we have an estimate of customer impact if we hit all three?
[04:52] Jordan L: ballpark — 20 to 35% reduction in P95 token latency for heavily cached workloads, and observed cost improvements because we avoid repeated recomputation. Those numbers are conservative.
[05:20] Samira K: also planning to add a transparency header in incident emails that shows what fallback model was used when we degraded, customers asked for that.
[05:45] Speaker 3: applause clap.
[06:10] Liam O'Neill: on Dedicated sales motion: new tiering will allow simpler on/off ramp for customers to move from hosted to reserved with a 90-day pilot credit. Also clarifying our SLA language around throughput and region failover. Concern raised by field — when do we allow model pinning?
[06:48] Maya P: model pinning for Dedicated is supported, but for hosted we recommend flexible routing and fallback for regional capacity. For private we support exact pinning per customer's contract.
[07:10] Ethan R: there's a tradeoff between cost and latency for pinned heavy models. We need to be intentional in sales collateral.
[07:35] Jordan L: technical deep-dive will be scheduled; i'll host an office hours for SEs to get the kernel selection and quantization notes. We'll mis-transcribe quantization sometimes as 'quantize a shun' in notes, so watch for typos.
[08:20] Samira K: product: Console updates — new dashboards for token-level cost, route-level error breakdowns, and a rollout UI for canaries. We plan an internal beta in two weeks and public docs the week after that.
[08:55] Ethan R: any blockers for beta?
[09:05] Maya P: mostly instrumentation and a couple of UX polish items. We will not hold launch for minor polish; the telemetry is the blocker.
[09:35] Speaker 4: question about retention policies.
[09:45] Samira K: retention — default hosted retention remains 30 days, enterprise can opt-in for longer with KMS/HSM integrations. For private deployments, retention is customer-managed.
[10:20] Ethan R: security review — we shipped the updated SOC 2 artifacts last week and a few customers flagged an ask for ISO 27001. People — legal and security will scope the gap analysis.
[10:50] Maya P: we also need to tighten audit logs for Dedicated; Ops will send a plan.
[11:20] Jordan L: tech note — the smart routing code now supports region-based fallback; some early tests show a 12% reduction in failed requests during simulated outages. We still need more load testing.
[12:00] Ethan R: okay, hiring. Headcount update — we're green for the quarter but we're pacing hires to the highest leverage areas: runtime, SE, and product. People Ops to open up a leadership review nomination for internal promotion.
[12:40] Speaker 5: can we get more details on compensation adjustments?
[12:50] Ethan R: compensation and bands we'll share with managers this week.
[13:10] Samira K: customer communication — we will send a short note to the top-30 customers about roadmap and what to expect from Console and Dedicated pricing. Jordan will own technical appendices.
[13:40] Jordan L: yep, i'll draft and circulate a version for review.
[14:05] Ethan R: open Q&A — please raise your hand in the chat.
[14:20] Speaker 6: question — with competitors like MegaCloudAI pushing aggressive Committed-use discounts, are we planning matching or differentiating on features?
[14:40] Liam O'Neill: we'll not go to the race-to-the-bottom on price; our argument is predictable throughput, observability, and private deployment options. We will add targeted promotional credits for pilots.
[15:05] Maya P: plus, our Runtime optimizations give us a technical advantage in throughput per GPU; we should lean on that in technical decks.
[15:30] Ethan R: finance — what's the margin impact of the new Dedicated tiers?
[15:40] Speaker 7 (Finance): modeled two scenarios; one keeps higher margins with tighter commit levels, the other lower margins but faster adoption. We'll recommend a middle path.
[16:05] Jordan L: ops note — to reduce incident frequency we need improved tracing hooks in the SDK; that is an engineering priority.
[16:25] Samira K: product note — we will run a small pilot (5 customers) for the canary rollout UI to gather real feedback before wider release.
[17:00] Ethan R: community and open source engagement — we have a maintainer summit scheduled; this helps with model onboarding and verifying performance on public models.
[17:25] Speaker 8: suggestion to beef up the benchmarking suite.
[17:40] Jordan L: agree, benchmarking should include variable seq lengths and mixed-precision runs; this will help us recommend quantization profiles in Optimize.
[18:10] Maya P: question — are we delaying any major features for Q2 because of the reliability sprint?
[18:22] Samira K: we're re-phasing a couple of lower-impact features but shipping Console core telemetry remains on schedule.
[18:50] Ethan R: quick remote shoutouts — Thanks to infra for the overnight work last week and to the SEs who helped customers during the incident.
[19:20] Speaker 9: applause.
[20:00] Ethan R: recap — engineering focuses: KV cache eviction, autoscaling signals, index warmup. Product: Console beta and rollout UI. Sales: Dedicated tiers and pilot credits. Security: SOC 2 artifacts and ISO gap analysis. People: nomination form and hiring cadence. Action owners listed in the follow-up.
[20:45] Jordan L: i'll post the technical deep-dive invite for next Tuesday and an office hours schedule.
[21:05] Maya P: i'll post the incident FAQ and the runbook doc link.
[21:20] Samira K: product will publish the Console roadmap doc by next Monday.
[21:40] Ethan R: final — what risks should we surface to the board next week? Major items: incident frequency, Dedicated revenue ramp, and private deployment compliance needs.
[22:05] Liam O'Neill: add sales pipeline uptake risk if we delay pricing clarity.
[22:30] Ethan R: great. Thanks everyone. We will follow up with the action list and a short recording.
[22:50] Speaker 10: bye all.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., V P C, K V cache, quantize a shun) consistent with typical automated captions. The meeting ran through a condensed 22-minute live chat portion followed by Q&A and ratified next steps; the recording length includes pre/post meeting hold for company-wide join and a short post debrief.

End of transcript.
